`db.tools` provides connection, query and SQL-file helpers for DBI applications.

The core operations use the caller's DBI driver. H2 restoration is an optional backend described in [H2 SQL backups](h2.html).

## Load the examples

```{r resources}
# Load the public API.
library(db.tools)
# Locate the packaged connection configuration and SQL query.
resources_directory <- system.file("examples", "survey", package = "db.tools")
# Select the H2 connection configuration.
configuration_file <- file.path(resources_directory, "database.yaml")
# Read the parameterized SQL statement.
sql <- read_sql_file(file.path(resources_directory, "queries", "numbers.sql"))
```

The YAML reads the H2 JDBC URL from `SURVEY_H2_URL`.

Download the original files from [Package resources](resources.html).

## Query through a scoped connection

Install RJDBC and withr, then set `H2_JAR` to the path of a compatible H2 JAR.

The example sets the URL from a temporary path. H2 creates the database when the provider opens the connection.

```{r query, eval=file.exists(Sys.getenv("H2_JAR")) && requireNamespace("RJDBC", quietly=TRUE)}
local({
  driver <- RJDBC::JDBC("org.h2.Driver", Sys.getenv("H2_JAR"), identifier.quote = '"')
  # Clean up the temporary directory and restore the environment when the example ends.
  directory <- withr::local_tempdir()
  database_url <- paste0("jdbc:h2:file:", file.path(directory, "survey"), ";DATABASE_TO_LOWER=TRUE")
  withr::local_envvar(c(SURVEY_H2_URL = database_url))

  connection_provider <- function() db_connect_from_yaml(driver, configuration_file)
  with_db_connection(connection_provider, function(connection) {
    DBI::dbWriteTable(connection, "numbers", data.frame(amount = 1:5))
    db_query(connection, sql, params = list(2))
  })
})
```

`db_query()` returns a `data.table`, preserving the result supplied by the database driver.

The driver defines placeholder syntax and supported bound parameter types.

`db_query()` accepts `params` for RJDBC connections and passes the values to the driver.

`with_db_connection()` calls the provider to open the connection and closes it when the callback finishes.

Do not supply a shared connection whose lifecycle belongs to another component.

When calling `db_query()` with an existing connection directly, the caller remains responsible for closing it.

## Connection configuration and secrets

The YAML document is a nonempty mapping of arguments passed to `DBI::dbConnect()`.

The caller supplies the driver separately. A YAML `drv` entry is rejected.

```yaml
host: localhost
port: 5432
dbname: survey
user: survey_reader
password: !env SURVEY_DB_PASSWORD
```

`!env` names a process environment variable and resolves its value when opening the connection.

Unset variables raise an error. Keep passwords outside configuration files and source code.

Applications may retrieve the value from a keyring at the start of an R session.

```{r keyring, eval=FALSE}
# Register a password through the keyring's secure interactive prompt.
keyring::key_set("survey-db")
# Supply the secret to this session under the name referenced by YAML.
Sys.setenv(SURVEY_DB_PASSWORD = keyring::key_get("survey-db"))
# Remove the process variable when database work finishes.
Sys.unsetenv("SURVEY_DB_PASSWORD")
```

The keyring entry has its own lifetime; the environment variable belongs only to the current process.

CI and services can supply the same variable through their secret manager.

## SQL resources

`read_sql_file()` reads UTF-8 text from an explicit path and preserves line boundaries.

It does not interpolate parameters, execute SQL or search an implicit working directory.

Use `system.file()` to locate resources bundled with an installed package.

## H2 backups

Use `h2_backup_connection_provider()` to supply connections from a trusted plain or compressed H2 SQL backup.

The [H2 guide](h2.html) covers destination directories, reuse, cleanup and driver settings.
